newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds close lower.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds close lower.

text.p: Israeli unlinked and dollar-linked bonds closed slightly lower on Tuesday amid profit taking, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): -0.07 pct to 102.82
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 pct to 101.84.
Volume was a moderate 142 million shekels with trading in the Makams falling to only 35 million shekels.
"Bond yields have fallen sharply since the beginning of the year and I don't think it is logical any longer to invest in them," said Yoram Ben-Yaeir at Ahrayut Investment Management.
"I believe that in the near term we will see a correction in yields as investors take profits," he added.

But a trader at Israel Discount Bank said bond prices could still move a little higher. "Yields on CPI-linked bonds have reached 4.1 percent and I think that they will continue to decline to around four percent. At this level prices are expected to stabilise," he said.
Unlinked bonds closed slightly lower due to profit-taking, with yields reaching 14.3-15 percent.
Traders said Makams rose mildly with yields on the Makam for one year falling to only 13.6 percent.

"Dollar-linked bonds have risen very fast and (today) investors started taking profits. I believe that they will resume rising as the dollar continues its rally against the mark," the Discount trader said.
On Tuesday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3310 shekels against 3.3230 on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
